title: The Bell That Rang at Low Tide

storyPreview.title: The Bell That Rang at Low Tide
storyPreview.summary: When a celebrated harbor engineer vanishes during the unveiling of Tideglass Quay, the city’s new floodgate project is thrown into scandal. Moments before his disappearance, the old chapel bell rang out across the fogbound waterfront—despite its tower being locked, condemned, and supposedly empty. SirLocked and his companion must separate civic pageantry from hidden grudges, follow a trail of maritime oddities, and determine whether the engineer was taken, fled, or met with something more sinister.
storyPreview.setting: A rain-polished Victorian port city where new steamworks and old sailor superstitions collide. The investigation moves between a grand municipal ceremony, salt-stained warehouses, a derelict chapel tower, and the half-finished machinery beneath the quay.
storyPreview.openingIncident: During a public ribbon-cutting for Tideglass Quay, the harbor bell tolls three times through heavy fog. The crowd turns toward the abandoned chapel tower, and in that brief confusion the guest of honor, engineer Alaric Venn, disappears from a guarded platform. In his place are a cracked pocket compass, a smear of blue sealing wax, and a ceremonial speech with one sentence violently scratched out.
storyPreview.tone: Atmospheric, clever, and cooperative, with a balance of grounded deduction, nautical folklore, civic intrigue, and puzzle-like physical clues. The case should feel tense but not grim, inviting players to compare observations, challenge assumptions, and revisit locations as new meanings emerge.
storyPreview.playerPromise: Players will investigate a locked-location disappearance across four focused scenes, cross-check witness accounts against physical evidence, decode small environmental puzzles, and uncover how secrets buried in the harbor’s past threaten the city’s future—all without relying on guesswork or supernatural answers.
keyLocations: Venn’s drafting room at the Harbor Works Office
The fogbound warehouse row beneath Gull Street
suspectTeasers: Maribel Quince, the ambitious deputy commissioner whose career depends on the quay opening without scandal
Jonah Pike, a retired diver who claims the new floodgates disturb something better left beneath the silt
Celia Venn, the engineer’s estranged sister, recently seen arguing over a sealed family ledger
Tomas Reed, a charming newspaper illustrator who arrived early, sketched everything, and insists he noticed nothing important
Edda Krail, the chapel caretaker who keeps keys to a tower the city swears no one can enter
